sections.value:
**#155 after-deploy: zero recorded launches in a quiet window; traffic-bearing F82 proof remains owed.**

Reported deployment **8dbd551ea81d486b065485ef157fea8ea320e64d**, also canonical main at sample start. Daemon **PID 11030**, process start **2026-11-08 00:53:38 +10:00**, unchanged across both snapshots. Ping identifies a healthy `pij-rs 0.1.0`, not an embedded Git SHA; commit association follows the deployment report and checkout identity.

Two pings: **2026-11-08 00:58:06.717402 to 00:59:06.719744 +10:00**, **60.002054 s** monotonic elapsed.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Daemon launches | **124 to 124: +0, 0.000/s**, every populated site flat |
| `ps.uds-peer-start` | Absent from both site maps; no increment recorded |
| Daemon interval CPU | **7.67 CPU seconds / 60.002054 s = 12.78%** of one CPU |
| Daemon RSS | **133.13 to 133.81 MiB**, +0.69 MiB |
| Machine launches | **33.0/s**, separate 20-second `nice -n 19 just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` sample |
| Claude traffic in the window | **0 delivery outcome events, 0 successful UDS deliveries, 0 Claude job ACKs** |

Read-only store queries used the verified `spine_by_seat_kind_at` index for each Claude seat, including historical/tombstoned identities, over the half-open millisecond event window. They selected only delivery/outcome and job metadata, never message bodies or Claude keys. EXPLAIN confirms recipient/kind/time seeks rather than a global spine scan.

The outcome selector uses `payload.outcome.outcome`, not a nonexistent root `result` key. A later real `claude-uds` queued event (seq **4228801**, outside the window) is a positive control that the selector can detect traffic. The populated lifetime spawn counters likewise distinguish this from an empty/wrong ping map.

**Limit:** no Claude delivery exercised the new path during these 60 seconds. The historical F82 baseline had eight successful deliveries/four carriers and +40 ps launches in 60.007 s. This quiet window is not workload-matched and proves neither per-delivery savings nor live kernel/discovery counts. A later traffic-bearing reading is still needed; no synthetic traffic was injected.

The machine instrument's sampled **32.8/s** attribution is a lower bound: **24.3/s other**, **8.5/s gone before identification**, with no observed daemon-child contribution. It made **262,000 in-process polls** in 20 seconds, so the niced observer is itself CPU work. Its 20-second scope differs from the daemon's 60-second site/CPU window. Rolling ps CPU values (7.4/10.4%) were not substituted for interval CPU.

Raw receipts retained in the session: `pr155-after-window.json`, `pr155-after-machine.json`, `pr155-after-delivery-evidence.json`. No build, test, restart, credential read or injected/model traffic.
